about.zmksDescription: ZMKs Studio is a community build based on ZMK Studio. It keeps the upstream ZMK Studio keymap editing workflow and adds this fork's UI, lighting, localization, and desktop client improvements. The original ZMK Studio project and ZMK contributors remain the foundation of this work.
about.sponsorsDescription: ZMK Studio is made possible thanks to the generous donation of time from our contributors, as well as the financial sponsorship from the following vendors:

flavorDesc.holdPreferred: Fires the hold as soon as the term passes or another key is pressed. Best for modifiers.
flavorDesc.balanced: If you press and release another key while holding, it resolves to a hold; release this key first and it taps. Fits how most modifiers are used.
flavorDesc.tapPreferred: Only holds if you truly keep it pressed past the term. Fewest typing misfires.
flavorDesc.tapUnlessInterrupted: Taps by default, holds only when interrupted by another key.

desc.retroTap: Held past the term without pressing another key? Still send the tap on release.
desc.holdWhileUndecided: Activate the hold immediately while deciding instead of waiting. Useful for mouse modifiers.
desc.holdWhileUndecidedLinger: Keep the hold active until just after the tap is sent. Only matters with Immediate Hold.
desc.holdTriggerOnRelease: Delay the positional hold decision until the key is released.
desc.quickTapMs: Press the key again within this time after a tap to tap again — e.g. tap-then-hold Backspace to repeat.
desc.requirePriorIdleMs: If you pressed another key within this time, resolve to a tap — avoids accidental holds while typing fast.

conn.title: Connection
conn.subtitle: View connection status and manage pairing between the keyboard and a 2.4G dongle.
conn.rpcNoResult: The firmware returned no reply for that request.
conn.noState: The firmware returned no connection state.
conn.unsupportedTitle: This firmware has no connection management
conn.unsupportedBody: Unable to read. Check the firmware version.
conn.unsupportedNote: The dongle section still works — it talks to the dongle over its own serial port, not to the keyboard firmware.
conn.switchOk: Switched. The keyboard is sending on the new link.
conn.switchPendingBody: The radio is restarting. This Studio connection drops as soon as it does — reconnect when the keyboard is back.
conn.switchDetachedBody: Disconnected. Reconnect to carry on setting the keyboard up.
conn.switch2g4Confirm: This switches the radio away from the link Studio is using. Studio disconnects for certain.
conn.usbNoCable: No USB data cable detected. The keyboard only really runs on the wire once the cable is in — in ZMK, a plugged USB link wins unless wireless was picked by hand.
conn.usbDropsStudio: Studio is on Bluetooth right now, so switching to USB shuts the radio link down and this connection drops. Reconnect over USB afterwards.
conn.usbKeepsStudio: Studio is already on USB — switching back to wired does not disturb it.
conn.bleDropsStudio: Studio is on Bluetooth right now. Selecting another slot or cancelling a pairing restarts the BLE link and this connection drops.
conn.bleKeepsStudio: Studio is on USB, so switching to Bluetooth does not disconnect it. The host still has to be paired with the keyboard to receive keystrokes.
conn.bleNoBondYet: No slot is paired yet — the keyboard will just start advertising.
conn.rf2g4Warning: Bluetooth and 2.4G share one radio, so switching restarts the radio stack (roughly 50 ms–1 s). The 2.4G link does not carry Studio RPC at all — switching to it always disconnects Studio; reconnect the cable afterwards.
conn.preferred2g4: 2.4G was picked manually, so the keyboard stays there. Plugging USB in still makes wired the preferred link.
conn.resultUsbRequired: The firmware refuses to leave USB while a USB cable is attached. Unplug the cable first, then switch.
conn.resultBusy: A radio switch is already running. Try again in a moment.
conn.resultUnsupported: This firmware does not have that link compiled in (the matching Kconfig option is off).
conn.resultInvalid: The firmware rejected that target link for this board.
conn.resultUnknown: Switch failed — the firmware returned an unrecognised result.
conn.bleDesc: Five slots. Pick an empty one, then search for the keyboard from the computer or phone you want to pair.
conn.bleSlotHintDrops: Studio is on Bluetooth: switching slots drops this connection.
conn.bleUnpairHint: Removes the bond stored in this slot. The host keeps its own copy until you delete the keyboard there too.
conn.bleUnpairAllHint: Clears all paired slots on the keyboard. Every host has to be paired again from scratch.
conn.blePairHint: To pair a new host: select an empty slot here, then start a Bluetooth scan on that computer or phone and pick the keyboard name.
conn.bleDropsStudioBody: Studio is connected over Bluetooth. Switching slots or unpairing restarts the BLE link and closes this connection — switching to an empty slot always does.
conn.bleNotSupported: This firmware was built without Bluetooth (CONFIG_ZMK_BLE is off).
conn.bleNoSlots: The firmware reported no Bluetooth slots.
conn.bleNoDetails: The firmware reports slots but did not return their details, so there is nothing to edit here.
conn.rfGenerateHint: The keyboard immediately jumps to the new key and address, so the current 2.4G link goes dead until the same three values reach the dongle.
conn.rfClearHint: Drops the stored key and address on the keyboard. A paired dongle stops hearing it until both ends are paired again.
conn.rfNewKeyNote: This pairing key is displayed once. Copy it or send it to the dongle.
conn.rfAtCommandNote: Paste this into the dongle's serial port at 115200 baud, or use «Pair both ends at once» below when the dongle is connected here.
conn.rfNotSupported: This firmware has no zmk.pairing subsystem, so pairing cannot be generated from here. Rebuild with the pairing handler enabled, or pair with the keyboard's own 2.4G binding.
conn.pairErrorGenerate: The keyboard did not return a usable pairing.
conn.pairErrorNoKeyboard: The keyboard is not connected, so no pairing could be generated.
conn.pairErrorAtArgs: The dongle rejected the AT+PAIR arguments (wrong length or non-hex). Nothing was written.
conn.pairErrorStorage: The dongle could not store the key (ERROR STORAGE) — it rolled back to the factory identity.
conn.pairErrorNoAt: That dongle firmware has no AT+PAIR handler (built without CONFIG_ZMK_2G4_DONGLE).
conn.pairErrorVerify: The read-back does not match the keyboard. The link will not come up until it does.
conn.pairStepGenerate: Pairing information generated on the keyboard
conn.pairStepAtPair: Pairing information written to the dongle
conn.pairOk: The keyboard and dongle are paired. Switch the keyboard to 2.4G to start using it.
conn.dongleDesc: Connect the keyboard and dongle over USB, then pair them in one click. No AT commands are needed.
conn.dongleUnsupported: This browser exposes no Web Serial API (Firefox and Safari do not), so the dongle cannot be reached from here. Use Chrome or Edge — or the desktop client — to pair the 2.4G link from Studio.
conn.dongleUnsupportedShort: This browser has no Web Serial support.
conn.dongleCancelled: Port selection was cancelled — nothing was opened.
conn.dongleOpenFailed: Could not open the serial port
conn.dongleLost: The dongle's serial port disappeared. Plug it back in and reconnect.
conn.dongleLostHint: The dongle dropped off the bus — unplugged, or it rebooted after AT+RST / AT+BL. Plug it back in and use «Reconnect»; the granted port is reused without a new picker.
conn.dongleClosesOnLeave: The port is held only while this page is open — coming back needs «Connect dongle» again, without a new picker.
conn.dongleNoStatus: Connect the dongle to read its pairing status.
conn.donglePairHint: The keyboard and dongle receive the same key and address automatically. The 2.4G link may disconnect briefly while they restart.
conn.donglePairBothHint: The keyboard jumps to the new pair immediately, so the existing 2.4G link dies until the dongle accepts the same values.
conn.donglePairNeedsPort: Connect the dongle first, then pair or clear the pairing.
conn.dongleClearBothHint: Clears the keyboard's key/address and sends AT+CLEAR to the dongle. The 2.4G link stays down until both are paired again.
conn.dongleClearDongleFailed: The dongle did not confirm AT+CLEAR
conn.atNotOpen: The dongle's serial port is not open.
conn.atTimeout: No answer within a few seconds. Check the dongle has compatible AT firmware and that nothing else holds the port.
conn.atResetHint: Reboots the dongle; the serial port closes and has to be reconnected.
conn.atBootloaderHint: Reboots the dongle into DFU/bootloader. It leaves the serial port until you flash it again or power-cycle it out of bootloader.
conn.dongleOpenSourceNote: The open-source 52840 dongle (ph_lite-dongle) supports the same AT pairing commands as the 52820. Generate on the keyboard first, then connect the receiver and write and verify the pairing state.
conn.rfNoRpc: The link is on 2.4G, which has no Studio RPC. Switch to USB or Bluetooth above, then come back.
conn.rfLocked: The keyboard is locked, so it refuses to hand out a pairing key. Unlock it with its own gesture first.
conn.rfRejected: The keyboard refused the pairing request — 2.4G pairing only runs while the link is on USB.

combos.priorIdleDesc: Only trigger if no other key was tapped shortly before the combo's first key.
combos.slowReleaseDesc: Release the combo when the last key is released, instead of the first.
combos.layersDesc: Layers this combo is active on. With none selected, it works on every layer.

combos.allReservedHint: Every combo slot on this keyboard is reserved by firmware. The unlock shortcut is managed from the Device page.

motion.emptyHint: No motion sensor was detected on this device, or the firmware has the motion subsystem disabled.

carry.title: Carry sleep
carry.desc: Enters sleep after sustained motion to reduce unintended input during transport.
carry.activeHint: The keyboard enters sleep when sustained motion meets the configured conditions.
carry.idleHint: Sustained motion is evaluated against the configured threshold and duration.
carry.motionDurationHint: Motion must persist for the configured duration before sleep. Brief vibration does not trigger sleep; key input cancels the pending transition.
carry.calibrateHint: Move the keyboard and observe the stable motion range. Use the lower end of that range as a starting threshold.

stillWake.title: Stationary wake
stillWake.desc: After a motion wake event, confirm that the device is stationary before keeping it awake.
stillWake.settleDurationHint: After a motion wake event, the keyboard must remain stationary for this duration; otherwise it returns to sleep.
stillWake.meterHint: Stationary confirmation uses motion state rather than a threshold marker.

tap.title: Tap detection
tap.desc: Trigger actions by tapping the case. Configure single and double taps separately for each side.
tap.windowHint: When both actions are configured on the same side, the single-tap action waits until this window ends so a double tap can take priority.
tap.layersHint: Respond to taps only on the selected active layers. No selection enables all layers.
tap.calibrateHint: Tap the case and observe the peak magnitude. Set the threshold slightly below valid tap peaks while remaining above normal typing vibration.

test.title: Tap test
test.hint: Tap the case to inspect detection results and calibrate parameters.
test.disabled: Tap detection is disabled. Enable it to inspect sensor events.
test.eventCount: sensor event count; a double tap may include single- and double-tap events
test.sideNote: Side detection follows the sensor direction signal. The physical direction depends on sensor mounting and firmware configuration.

unlockPanel.title: Unlock shortcut
unlockPanel.desc: The keyboard locks itself so a web page can't change your keymap without you. Unlocking is always a physical action — Studio cannot do it remotely.
unlockPanel.protectedHint: Firmware reserves this slot for unlocking, so it can't be repointed at another behavior.
unlockPanel.noneDesc: This firmware exposes no studio unlock binding. Once the keyboard locks, Studio won't be able to edit it again — reflash before locking it.
unlockPanel.changeHint: You'll be asked to perform the new gesture before it replaces the current one, and the keyboard stays unlocked throughout.
unlockPanel.noSpareSlot: Setting up a combo shortcut needs one free combo slot to confirm the gesture with. Free a slot on the Combos page first.
unlockPanel.createHint: Sets up a key combination that unlocks the keyboard, alongside the existing unlock key. You'll be asked to perform it once before it's saved.

unlockChange.title: Change unlock shortcut
unlockChange.pickHint: Click the keys the shortcut should use — at least two, pressed together.
unlockChange.noLayout: No physical layout reported, so keys can't be picked.
unlockChange.warnConflict: Another combo already uses exactly these keys. Pick a different set.
unlockChange.warnTyping: These are all ordinary keys, so the chord could fire while typing. Studio will require a brief pause before it counts — including one layer or modifier key is safer.
unlockChange.pressHint: Your current shortcut is untouched until this one is confirmed, and the keyboard stays unlocked throughout — so nothing is at risk if it doesn't work.
unlockChange.confirmedHint: The keyboard produced the test keystroke, so this gesture works. Apply it as the unlock shortcut?
unlockChange.timeoutSafe: You can apply without confirmation; this keyboard still has another way to unlock.
unlockChange.timeoutRisky: Applying without confirmation means that if the gesture doesn't work, the keyboard can't be edited again without reflashing.
unlockChange.doneHint: It's live right now, but only in memory — write it to the keyboard or it's gone at the next power cycle.
unlockChange.priorIdleApplied: A brief pause is now required before the chord counts, so it can't fire while typing.
unlockChange.warnUnverified: Applied without confirmation — test it before you let the keyboard lock.
unlockChange.errArm: Couldn't set up the test. Nothing was changed.
unlockChange.errCommit: Writing the new shortcut failed. Your old one still works.
unlockChange.errNoKeyPress: This firmware has no Key Press behavior, so the gesture can't be tested.
unlockChange.timeoutNoInput: No keystrokes are reaching Studio at all. Make sure this window has focus and that the keyboard is typing into this computer.
unlockChange.tryAnotherProbe: Retry with a different test key
unlockChange.timeoutSwallowed: If pressing them together shows nothing at all, the combo IS firing — ZMK swallows the keys it consumes and sends the test key instead, so only the test key is going missing. Try a different one. (Seeing the keys individually just means the chord didn't complete.)
unlockChange.errStoredBehavior: Firmware accepted the test but didn't store the test keystroke on the slot. That's why the chord swallows keys and emits nothing — the trigger landed and the behavior didn't. This needs a firmware fix; the read-back above is the evidence.
unlockChange.errStoredPositions: Firmware accepted the test but stored different trigger keys, so this device isn't taking the write as sent.
unlockChange.pickHintCreate: Your existing unlock key stays as it is, so this is purely an addition.
unlockChange.warnOverlap: These keys are also used by another combo
unlockChange.warnOverlapHint: Overlapping combos compete, and the other one may win — which makes the test below look like it failed for no reason.
unlockChange.warnSameAsCurrent: That's the shortcut already in use, so there's nothing to confirm. Pick different keys — or cancel to keep it as it is.
unlockChange.warnShadowedByUnlock: These keys overlap your current unlock shortcut, which stays live during the test. It would win the chord and unlock instead of producing the test keystroke, so the test can't confirm anything. Pick keys it doesn't share.
unlockChange.savedOk: Written to the keyboard — firmware reports the shortcut on the slot.
unlockChange.savedVerifyHint: Studio can't see storage, only the live slot. Worth unplugging the keyboard and reconnecting once to confirm it stuck — while your old unlock method still works.
unlockChange.savedFailed: The save didn't take — firmware doesn't report the shortcut on the slot afterwards. Don't let this keyboard lock until you've used your existing unlock method to check it.
